source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.taxon_division: Flora distinguishes two intergrading subspecies by peduncle elongation timing, raceme flower number and leaflet counts
morphology_source_reported.diagnostics: subsp. leavenworthii: early opening before peduncle extension, typically (7–)11–15(–17) leaflets; subsp. ludoviciana: after peduncle extension, 7–10(–13) leaflets
morphology_source_reported.genus_level_field_signs: Vetch tendrils at rachis tips, once-pinnate leaves, unwinged stems [genus account, p.706]; not uniquely diagnostic for V. ludoviciana
morphology_source_reported.flora_species_key: Racemes 1–19 flowered, corollas 4–8 mm; 1–2 flowered racemes may still key to V. ludoviciana if leaves with 8–18 leaflets [p.707]

habitat_source_reported: Varies by subspecies: rocky, clayey or sandy prairies and roadsides / rocky or sandy woods and roadsides
cautions: Subspecies intergrade in 1999 Flora and repository also has variety-level entries; preserve ranks and reconcile before using identification traits
Taxon concepts require independent name reconciliation before identification scoring
Regional occurrence is not evidence of local BONAP nativity
Do not incorrectly exclude 1–2-flowered Vicia ludoviciana based on the first key branch listing 3–19 flowers; the later branch includes 1–2-flowered plants.
